source.snippet: I am trying to create a forwarding-only email address in my MS 365 tenant, but not having any luck. I have my mail for mydomain.org hosted at MS365; I have mail for lists.mydomain.org hosted with another mail provider (used for mailing lists). I can successfully send email to/from mylist@lists.mydomain.com. I have a connector set up mydomain.org to lists.mydomain.org: 'Only when I have a transport rule set up that redirects messages to this connector'.

problem_statement: IT administrators managing Microsoft 365 tenants struggle to configure simple email forwarding-only addresses across mixed mail providers, requiring non-obvious combinations of connectors, transport rules, and shared mailboxes — a task that should be trivial but is not.
target_segment: IT administrators and MSPs managing Microsoft 365 tenants for small-to-mid-size businesses with hybrid or multi-provider email setups
notes: Business context: IT admins and MSPs are paid to manage M365 tenants; configuration complexity wastes billable hours. Repeated pattern across M365 admin forums. A guided configuration tool or runbook SaaS for common M365 mail routing scenarios could be sold to MSPs on a per-seat or per-tenant basis.
